call_summary: Caller wanted to reschedule a Thursday 2 PM appointment; the agent could only find a Monday 9/14 10 AM appointment, never located the Thursday slot, and ended the call with the existing Monday appointment unchanged and no new booking made. Along the way the agent invented a date of birth, ignored the caller's correction to it, and disclosed appointment details without any identity verification.

findings.title: Fabricated the patient's date of birth
findings.quote: Your demo patient profile is set up, and your date of birth is July 4, 2000.
findings.what_happened: The caller only provided a first and last name, yet the agent asserted a specific date of birth it had never been given or confirmed.
findings.why_it_matters: Stating unverified demographic data as fact can attach the wrong DOB to a chart, cause mismatched records, and undermine any downstream identity checks.
findings.expected: Ask the caller for their date of birth and read it back for confirmation rather than asserting one.

findings.title: Lost the caller's correction to their date of birth
findings.quote: I see you have a follow-up appointment scheduled for Monday, September 14th at 10:00 AM with Doogie Howser
findings.what_happened: The caller explicitly corrected the DOB to July 9, 1975, and the agent never acknowledged, confirmed, or updated it — it moved straight to appointment lookup.
findings.why_it_matters: An uncorrected DOB stays wrong in the record and may have caused the agent to search the wrong patient chart, which could explain the missing Thursday appointment.
findings.expected: Acknowledge the correction, confirm the new DOB back to the caller, update the profile, and re-run the appointment lookup against the corrected identity.

findings.title: Disclosed appointment details without identity verification
findings.quote: I see you have a follow-up appointment scheduled for Monday, September 14th at 10:00 AM with Doogie Howser at Nashville 220 Athens Way.
findings.what_happened: On the strength of a self-reported first and last name alone — with an unverified, agent-invented DOB on file — the agent read out provider, date, time, and clinic location.
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone who knows a patient's name could obtain their appointment and provider details; this is a PHI disclosure risk.
findings.expected: Verify at least two identifiers (e.g., DOB and phone number or address) against the record before revealing or changing any appointment.

findings.title: Dropped the caller's request to book a new Monday morning appointment
findings.quote: Let me try searching for Monday morning appointments again. You already have a follow-up appointment booked for Monday, September 14 at 10:00 a.m. Would you like to keep this appointment, reschedule it, or cancel it?
findings.what_happened: The caller asked to book a new follow-up for Monday morning and supplied the visit type; instead of returning availability, the agent pivoted back to the existing appointment and never offered any open slots.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller's actual booking request went unfulfilled and the call ended with no new appointment, so the reschedule scenario was never completed.
findings.expected: Search and present actual Monday morning availability for a follow-up, and separately clarify whether the caller wants that in addition to or instead of the existing 9/14 slot.

findings.title: Dead-ended the missing-appointment problem with no escalation path
findings.quote: I don't see any Thursday appointment in your records. So there's nothing to cancel for that day.
findings.what_happened: After repeated failed lookups for the Thursday 2 PM appointment, the agent simply concluded nothing existed and closed out without offering a staff callback or transfer.
findings.why_it_matters: If the Thursday appointment does exist under a variant record, the caller becomes a no-show and the slot is wasted; the caller left believing it was handled.
findings.expected: Offer to transfer to or take a message for front-desk staff to manually search for the Thursday booking before asserting it doesn't exist.

findings.title: Ignored the caller's stated reason for calling and repeated the profile prompt
findings.quote: I can help with that. Would you like to create a demo patient profile first? I just need your first and last name to get started.
findings.what_happened: The caller stated they had a Thursday appointment to reschedule; the agent acknowledged generically and re-asked the same profile-creation question it had just asked.
findings.why_it_matters: Restating the scripted prompt instead of engaging with the request makes the agent feel unresponsive and lengthens the call.
findings.expected: Acknowledge the reschedule request specifically and explain that a name is needed to pull up the existing appointment.
